newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks expected to continue volatility.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks expected to continue volatility.

text.p: * Toronto stocks were expected to continue their volatility at the open on Friday. * Analysts said that gains in banking and other interest-sensitive stocks would help offset losses.
Toronto's stock market was expected to continue to underperform U.S. markets at the open on Friday, with analysts predicting some strength in banking and other interest rate-sensitive stocks.
"Our market has acted with much less vigor than the U.S. market," one analyst said. "Our market has been very lethargic in the last 10 days."
The analyst said that comments earlier this week by Bank of Canada Governor Gordon Thiessen and a resulting weaker Canadian dollar might help offset any downward trend in Canadian markets.
Thiessen told a press conference following a speech in Quebec City that the Bank of Canada had room to maneuver in the face of future U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate hikes.
The comments were interpreted by some traders as an indication that the central bank would not match the next Fed hike, triggering a sudden decline in the Canadian dollar.
"Thiessen's little chat weakened the dollar off, and that seemed to help people's thoughts that interest rates will not go up," the trader said.
"That should be good for the banks and the interest-sensitive stocks," the trader added.
* Investors are eying Cineplex-Odeon Corp, which jumped on Thursday on published reports that the theater operator is in merger talks with Sony Corp's Loews Theaters arm.
